summary: Independent review of the zero-record labelling follow-up, which closes the finding I recorded when pinning #967: the Tracebacks row rendered PASS with no condition on its denominator, so zero tracebacks out of zero scanned records read as a clean pass. I came into this review expecting the fix might be cosmetic, because a label is not a gate, and I checked that directly rather than assuming either way. It is partly cosmetic by design: services_without_records feeds only the row status text and is never appended to failures, so a zero-record service still exits 0 and the gate still goes green. But I mutated the tool to append it to failures and that turned a test RED, because test coverage explicitly pins the string '0 failed checks / 9 reported checks' for a PARTIAL_N/A run. So the non-failing behaviour is a deliberate, covered design decision rather than an oversight, which is the answer I needed before objecting to it. On the evidence I now agree it is the right call. I ran the head version of the tool READ-ONLY against the real box from /tmp, without touching the deployment, which stayed at 5dae7c9a with a clean tree, and removed the temporary files afterwards. That run shows the two services that actually matter are measured against genuine denominators: schwab-1m-v2 0/24403 and oms 0/21241 timestamped records, with only reconciler at N/A(0/0), and reconciler is the known-quiet service whose log has been 0 bytes since 2026-08-28. Restarted services now reads PASS 3/3 and Services not restarted PASS 6/6, so my 09-12 oms and reconciler restarts are fully attested. The only failing rows are REST warmup and BOOT-HOLD release, both Monday-dependent because Sunday has no scanner watchlist. Failing the entire gate on a permanently quiet service would make Monday's gate red every day and push toward bypassing it, which is a worse outcome than an honest PARTIAL_N/A. I also note approvingly that the summary line changed from 'measured checks' to 'reported checks': not every reported row was measured, and the previous wording claimed otherwise. Mutation matrix, 3 mutations against a baseline of 37 green: removing the PARTIAL_N/A label so a zero-record service reads PASS again turned 1 test RED; inverting the zero-record detection turned 1 RED; and appending the zero-record services to failures turned 1 RED, which is the mutation that proved the design is intentional. Controlled pair, full unit suite, sorted failure-NAME sets: base c94caa88 46 failed / 3775 passed, head af13e89f 46 failed / 3776 passed, identical 46 names, zero new failures, and the +1 delta is exactly the one new test, so the numbers reconcile without residue. The base also matches #967's head exactly, as it should since c94caa88 is #967 merged. Both worktrees were asserted to import their own project_mai_tai before any count was trusted. Base is an ancestor of head and the diff is confined to the tool and its test file. FOLLOW-UP FINDING, recorded rather than blocked. Because the reconciler is permanently quiet, this row will read PARTIAL_N/A on every single run forever. If oms or schwab-1m-v2 ever goes silent, the row STATUS is identical and the exit code is unchanged; the only tell is an additional service name appearing inside the detail string. An always-on N/A habituates the reader, and a newly-silent service is then indistinguishable from the routine one at the level anybody actually reads. The clean fix is the same shape the known-defect watch already uses for UNARMED rows: declare which services are EXPECTED to be quiet, so that an unexpected silence is distinguishable from the expected one and can be made to fail. Not a merge blocker, since the detail string does name the affected services and the trading-relevant services are genuinely measured today. Operational note carried forward from the #967 pin: the post-merge sequence must explicitly update EXPECTED_SHA inside preopen.sh when the checkout is synced, because it currently pins 5dae7c9a; syncing without that makes Monday's gate fail on checkout identity rather than on anything real. EXPECTED_PID 1089323 and EXPECTED_START 2026-09-12 20:34:27 UTC remain correct and the sync must not restart any service. CI: validate to be confirmed before I use the word pinned.
